chapter_name: Information and Communication Technology Skills - II
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how operating systems work, master file management, protect your computer from digital threats, and learn essential online security practices!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An OS (like Windows, Linux, Android) acts as an interface between the user and computer hardware. It manages memory, processes, files, hardware devices, and system security.
Organizing files into logical folder hierarchies, naming conventions, and understanding file extensions (.docx, .jpg, .mp3) to retrieve data efficiently.
Malicious software includes Viruses (attach to files), Worms (self-replicate across networks), Trojans (disguised as useful software), and Spyware (secretly track user activity).
Keep systems healthy by installing updated Antivirus software, using strong passwords, running Disk Cleanup and Defragmentation, and taking regular data backups.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Extension Explorer
fun_activity.instructions: Open your computer or phone's file manager. Find three different files and check their file extensions (the letters after the dot, like .pdf or .png). Write down which application opens each extension!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between a Computer Virus (requires human action to run) and a Worm (replicates and spreads automatically).
📌 Know the difference between GUI (Graphical User Interface - icons/menus like Windows) and CUI (Character User Interface - text commands like MS-DOS).
📌 List 4 daily habits for physical computer maintenance (keeping liquids away, cleaning air vents, using a surge protector, shutting down properly).
quick_recap: ⭐ A Firewall monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic to block unauthorized access.
⭐ Temporary files should be deleted regularly to free up hard disk space and speed up the PC.
⭐ Phishing is a cybercrime where attackers use fake emails or websites to trick users into revealing passwords.
